Hi Alex — great to meet earlier today. Quick recap from our discovery call and a recommended next-step plan so your eng team can get started integrating Redwood:

- Primary use case: downstream document summarization + reranking for search results; goal is ~200ms median latency for short queries and cost-conscious embedding usage.
- Traffic pattern: low QPS now (proof-of-concept), expected steady growth as product ramps.
- Data constraints: customer PII filtered before sending; prefer hosted for speed but want Private/VPC conversation later.

Integration priorities we discussed:
1) SDK quickstart (Python + TypeScript) — local dev & sample app
2) Auth options — API key vs service account & short-lived creds for CI
3) Routing & model selection — latency vs cost policies, region pinning
4) Structured output / tool calling — for downstream parsers/actions
5) Embeddings & reranker strategy — index size, batching, cost tradeoffs
6) Local testing & env setup — Docker image and sample env scripts

Proposed next steps:
- I can share a preview org and sample repo access (see link below).

Alex — great questions, answered inline below. I've attached a mutual-action-plan (mutual-action-plan.xlsx) and added a HubSpot link to the deal.

> 1) Auth: we prefer short-lived creds tied to a service account (we rotate keys nightly). Do you support that pattern? Any example for CI/cd pipeline?
Yes — we support short-lived service account tokens via our IAM integration and several KMS providers. Typical CI pattern: create a service account with limited scopes, request a short-lived token from our token service (we provide an API) and inject it into your CI job. See example: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples/blob/main/finbuild/auth/ci-example.md

> 2) Embeddings cost: for our index (~2M vectors) any guidance on approximate monthly cost with batching and recommended dimension?
Estimated guidance (very approximate):
- If you use 1536-d vectors and batch embeddings at 256 items, expect lower per-unit cost due to batching; storage and retrieval costs dominate for 2M vectors. We'll provide a cost model in the deep-dive. We also recommend asymmetric reranking (dense + sparse) to reduce query-time ops.

> 3) Sample language: engineering will want Python first. Can you push a minimal Python sample that shows auth, embedding call, and a simple reranker RPC?
Yes — Dev is attaching a small env setup script and a Python snippet below. Full examples live in the repo.

Python quick snippet (minimal):

from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="<SHORT_LIVED_TOKEN>")
# embeddings
emb = client.embeddings.create(model="rw-emb-small", input=["doc text"])
# rerank (embedding + generation hybrid)
r = client.rerank.create(model="rw-rerank-v1", query="How do I...", candidates=["cand1","cand2"])

Mutual action plan (high level):
- Week 0: preview org + sample repo access, run quickstart locally (we help)
- Week 1: tech deep-dive (routing, auth, scaling) + integrate embeddings POC
- Week 2: reranker integration and basic QA; sample evaluation prompts and cost review

I've tentatively placed the deep-dive on Wed Jul 22 10:00am PST per your availability. Is that good?

Best,
Marissa

Thanks Alex — I'm Dev on the infra side, looping in Lukas who owns embeddings performance. Quick notes and an env script attached (env-setup.sh):

- Auth: we'll drop a short-lived token flow for your CI. Example: use the service-account-to-token endpoint, scope it to embeddings+rerank only.
- Local testing: use our dev Docker image (redwood/dev:latest) to run the SDK locally and exercise streaming responses. Example docker run:
  docker run --rm -e REDWOOD_API_KEY="<token>" -v $(pwd):/app -w /app redwood/dev:latest python3 samples/quickstart.py

- Routing & model variants: default policy in the sample app pins to us-west for latency; you can configure fallback to a cost tier (rw-small) for non-critical queries.

Attachments: env-setup.sh (attached), also pushed a minimal Python sample to the repo at https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples/tree/main/finbuild/python
